He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]] and was drafted by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the second round of the [[2014 NBA draft]]. Grant has also played for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], [[Denver Nuggets]], [[Detroit Pistons]] and [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He won a gold medal with the [[2020 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2020 U.S. Olympic team]]. ==High school career== Grant attended [[DeMatha Catholic High School]] in [[Hyattsville, Maryland]], where as a senior in 2011–12, he averaged 12.5 points in 23 games.[http://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/jerami-grant/8404-fTpEeKZ5AAmVebBJg/default.htm Jerami Grant's (Hyattsville, MD) High School Timeline] Considered a four-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], Grant was listed as the No. 11 power forward and the No. 37 player in the nation in 2012.[https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/118517 Jerami Grant Recruiting Profile] ==College career== [[File:Jerami Grant 2014 (cropped).jpg|upright|thumb|left|Grant at Syracuse in 2014]] At [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]], Grant averaged 12.1 points, 6.8 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 31.4 minutes per game in 2013–14 while shooting 49.6% from the floor; he also scored in double figures in 24 of 32 games played and posted 19 points three times. Further, he was a 2014 All-ACC Honorable Mention selection. In April 2014, Grant declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final two years of college eligibility.{{Cite magazine |last=Thamel |first=Pete |authorlink=Pete Thamel |date=April 14, 2014 |title=Syracuse sophomore forward Jerami Grant to enter NBA draft |url=https://www.si.com/college/2014/04/14/syracuse-orange-jerami-grant-nba-draft |access-date=August 1, 2023 |magazine=Sports Illustrated}} He started off as a guard, then moved to the small forward position. ==Professional career== ===Philadelphia 76ers (2014–2016)=== On June 26, 2014, Grant was selected in the second round of that year's [[2014 NBA draft|NBA draft]] with the 39th overall pick by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]],{{cite news |date=June 27, 2014 |title=Sixers Select McDaniels, Grant, Micic in the Second Round of the 2014 NBA Draft |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/140626-second-round |url-status=dead |access-date=June 27, 2014 |archive-date=January 14, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210114004000/https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/140626-second-round }} and he joined the team for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news |title=Sixers Announce Orlando Pro Summer League Camp Invitees|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/140701-opsl-camp-invitees|access-date=July 1, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2014}} On September 29, 2014, he signed a four-year deal with the franchise, with two of them being guaranteed.{{Cite web |url=https://thesixersense.com/2014/09/29/jerami-grant-signs-two-year-guaranteed-deal-sixers |title=Jerami Grant Signs Two-Year Guaranteed Deal with Sixers |access-date=August 1, 2023 |archive-date=September 30, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220930011205/https://thesixersense.com/2014/09/29/jerami-grant-signs-two-year-guaranteed-deal-sixers/ |url-status=dead }}[http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2014/09/philadelphia_76ers_sign_former_syracuse_forward_jerami_grant_to_2-year_deal.html Philadelphia 76ers sign former Syracuse forward Jerami Grant to 2-year deal] On January 21, 2015, he came away with eight blocks in a loss to the [[New York Knicks]]; this was the most blocks in a game for a 76er since [[Samuel Dalembert]] had nine on December 12, 2007, as well as the most by a 76er rookie since [[Shawn Bradley]] had nine on January 17, 1994.{{Cite web |last=Gelston |first=Dan |date=January 21, 2015 |title=Anthony helps Knicks to 2nd straight win, 98-91 over 76ers |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150121/NYKPHI/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160125185425/http://www.nba.com/games/20150121/NYKPHI/gameinfo.html |archive-date=January 25, 2016 |access-date=February 2, 2015 |website=NBA.com}} On February 2, he had a season-best game with 18 points and 7 rebounds in a loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/grantje01/gamelog/2015/ Jerami Grant 2014-15 Game Log] In July 2015, Grant re-joined the 76ers for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]]. On November 11, 2015, he recorded his first career [[double-double]] with 12 points and 10 rebounds, coming in a loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20151121062040/http://www.nba.com/gamenotes/sixers.pdf 76ers vs Hornets game notes] On December 30, he posted a then career-high 11 rebounds to go along with 16 points and five blocks in a 110–105 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{Cite web |last=Wagaman |first=Michael |date=December 31, 2015 |title=Sixers surprise Kings for 2nd win in 3 games |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151230/PHISAC/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161202131916/http://www.nba.com/games/20151230/PHISAC/gameinfo.html |archive-date=December 2, 2016 |access-date=December 31, 2015 |website=[[NBA.com]]}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2016–2019)=== On November 1, 2016, Grant was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for [[Ersan İlyasova]] and a protected draft pick.{{cite web |date=November 1, 2016 |title=Thunder Acquires Jerami Grant and Trade Exception |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/jerami-grant-161101 |access-date=August 1, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} He made his debut for the Thunder the following day in an 85–83 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], recording six points, two rebounds, and two blocks in 18 minutes off the bench.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899514|title=Westbrook gets 35, leads unbeaten Thunder past Clips 85-83|work=ESPN.com|date=November 2, 2016|access-date=November 5, 2016}} On December 19, 2016, he scored a season-high 15 points in a 110–108 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899857|title=Hawks overcome Westbrook's 46 to beat Thunder 110-108|work=ESPN.com|date=December 19, 2016|access-date=December 19, 2016}} On February 1, 2017, he tied his season high mark with 15 points in a 128–100 loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899433|title=Butler scores 28 and Bulls rout Thunder 128-100|work=ESPN.com|date=February 1, 2017|access-date=February 2, 2017}} [[File:Jerami Grant (32049656824) crop.jpg|thumb|right|Jerami Grant with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in 2017]] On October 31, 2017, Grant scored 17 points off the bench in a 110–91 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. He finished 5-of-9 from the floor to record 17 points for the first time since April 1, 2016.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974854|title=Paul George, Thunder cruise to 110-91 win over Bucks|work=ESPN.com|date=October 31, 2017|access-date=October 31, 2017}} On July 7, 2018, Grant re-signed with the Thunder on a three-year, $27 million contract.{{cite web |title=Thunder Signs Jerami Grant to Multi-Year Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/grant-180707|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 9, 2018|date=July 7, 2018}} On January 10, 2019, he scored a then career-high 25 points to go with 12 rebounds in a 154–147 double-overtime loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071295|title=Aldridge scores 56, Spurs outlast Thunder 154-147 in 2OT|work=ESPN.com|date=January 10, 2019|access-date=January 11, 2019}}{{cite web |last=Gallo|first=Nick|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/recap-spurs-190110|title=Double-OT Thriller A Show of Thunder's Heart – OKC 147, SAS 154|work=NBA.com|date=January 10, 2019|access-date=January 11, 2019}} On March 18, he scored 27 points in a 116–107 loss to the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071727|title=Dragic, Wade lead Heat past Westbrook-less Thunder, 116-107|work=ESPN.com|date=March 18, 2019|access-date=April 11, 2019}} On April 10, he set a then career high with 28 points in a 127–116 win over the Bucks.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071899|title=Thunder get 6th spot in West with win over Bucks|work=ESPN.com|date=April 10, 2019|access-date=April 11, 2019}} ===Denver Nuggets (2019–2020)=== On July 8, 2019, Grant was traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] for a 2020 first-round pick.{{cite web |title=Denver Nuggets acquire Jerami Grant from Oklahoma City Thunder|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-acquire-jerami-grant-from-thunder-070819|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 8, 2019|date=July 8, 2019}} [[File:Jerami Grant free throw (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Jerami Grant with the [[Denver Nuggets]] in 2020]] On February 25, 2020, Grant scored a then career-high 29 points in a 115–98 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2020/02/25/jerami-grant-career-high-nuggets-beat-pistons/|title = Jerami Grant's career-high 29 points paces Nuggets past Pistons|date = February 26, 2020}} On September 15, 2020, in a Game 7 win against the favored Clippers, Grant outscored [[Paul George]] 14 to 10 while playing 9 fewer minutes. However, he struggled against [[LeBron James]] and [[Anthony Davis]] in the Western Conference Finals, as the Nuggets fell to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in five games. Grant scored 26 points in the Nuggets' Game 3 victory.{{Cite web |url=https://www.hoop-ball.com/nba-fantasy-news-and-advice/fantasy-nba-player-news/jerami-grant-emerges-as-an-x-factor-in-game-3-posting-26-points-and-two-steals/|title = Jerami Grant emerges as an X-factor in Game 3, posting 26 points and two steals – Hoop-Ball|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210703003536/https://www.hoop-ball.com/nba-fantasy-news-and-advice/fantasy-nba-player-news/jerami-grant-emerges-as-an-x-factor-in-game-3-posting-26-points-and-two-steals/|archive-date=July 3, 2021}} Grant averaged 11.6 points and 3.3 rebounds in the playoffs. ===Detroit Pistons (2020–2022)=== On November 22, 2020, Grant signed a three-year, $60 million contract with the [[Detroit Pistons]] through a sign-and-trade with the [[Denver Nuggets]]. Detroit also received draft rights to [[2015 NBA draft|2015]] second-round pick [[Nikola Radičević]] in exchange for cash considerations.{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-jerami-grant-and-draft-rights-nikola-radicevic|title=Detroit Pistons Acquire Jerami Grant and Draft Rights to Nikola Radicevic|work=NBA.com|date=November 22, 2020}}{{Cite web |title=Pistons land Jerami Grant in sign-and-trade with Nuggets |url=https://www.nba.com/news/report-jerami-grant-agrees-to-big-deal-with-pistons|website=NBA.com |date=November 22, 2020 |access-date=November 22, 2020}} On February 17, 2021, Grant scored a then career-high 43 points in a 105–102 loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite web |title=Zach LaVine, Bulls rally from 25-point deficit to stun Pistons despite Jerami Grant's career game|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2021/02/17/detroit-pistons-game-jerami-grant-zach-lavine-chicago-bulls/6792187002/|access-date=2021-02-19|website=Detroit Free Press|language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Grant's 43 goes for naught in Pistons loss to Chicago – 'We just needed one more guy to step up'|url=https://www.nba.com/amp/pistons/features/grants-43-goes-naught-pistons-loss-chicago-we-just-needed-one-more-guy-step|access-date=2021-02-19|website=nba.com}} Grant ended the season as a [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|Most Improved Player]] award finalist, finishing second behind [[Julius Randle]], while averaging a career high in points per game.{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/features/2020-21-rewind-grants-breakout-season-ends-him-most-improved-player-finalist#|title=2020-21 Rewind: Grant's breakout season ends with him as a Most Improved Player finalist|website=NBA.com|last=Langlois|first=Keith|date=May 24, 2021|access-date=June 25, 2021}} On December 10, 2021, in a 93–109 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], Grant suffered a right thumb injury.{{Cite web |last=Rapp |first=Timothy |title=Pistons' Jerami Grant Reportedly out Indefinitely After Suffering Thumb Injury |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10020591-pistons-jerami-grant-reportedly-out-indefinitely-after-suffering-thumb-injury |access-date=March 21, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report}} On December 16, he underwent surgery to repair the [[ulnar collateral ligament]] (UCL) in his right thumb and was ruled out for at least six weeks.{{Cite web |date=December 18, 2021 |title=Jerami Grant has surgery, out indefinitely |url=https://www.nba.com/news/report-jerami-grant-out-indefinitely-with-torn-thumb-ligaments |access-date=March 21, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} On March 28, 2022, Grant was ruled out for the remainder of the season with a calf strain.{{Cite web |title=Detroit Pistons' Jerami Grant to miss rest of season with calf strain |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33618040|access-date=March 30, 2022 |website=ESPN|date=March 29, 2022 }} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2022–2026)=== On July 6, 2022, Grant was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], along with the draft rights to [[Ismaël Kamagate]], in exchange for a top-four protected 2025 first-round pick (via [[Milwaukee Bucks|Milwaukee]]), the draft rights to [[Gabriele Procida]], and two future second-round picks.{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2022 |title=Trail Blazers Acquire Jerami Grant In Trade With Detroit |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-acquire-jerami-grant-in-trade-with-detroit |access-date=July 7, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} On October 23, Grant put up 16 points, along with a game-winning layup in a 106–104 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/blazers-news-jerami-grants-go-ahead-game-winner-over-lebron-james-anthony-davis/|title=Jerami Grant's go-ahead game-winner over LeBron James, Anthony Davis|website=ClutchPoints|last=Silverman|first=Steve|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=October 23, 2022}} On November 4, Grant scored 30 points and hit a game-winning jumper in a 108–106 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/suns-news-jerami-grant-wild-buzzer-beater-for-blazers-has-nba-fans-angry-over-missed-traveling-call/|title=Jerami Grant's wild buzzer-beater for Blazers has Suns fans angry over missed traveling call|website=ClutchPoints|last=Guinhawa|first=Angelo|date=November 4, 2022|access-date=November 4, 2022}} On November 25, Grant scored a then career-high 44 points in a 132–129 overtime win over the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/blazers-news-jerami-grant-snatches-portland-history-with-unreal-44-point-explosion-at-msg|title=Jerami Grant snatches Blazers history with unreal 44-point explosion at MSG|website=ClutchPoints|last=Songco|first=Paolo|date=November 25, 2022|access-date=November 25, 2022}} On July 9, 2023, Grant re-signed with the Blazers on a five-year, $160 million contract.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Re-Sign Jerami Grant|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-re-sign-jerami-grant|website=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2023|access-date=July 9, 2023}} On February 8, 2024, Grant scored a career-high 49 points in a 128–122 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|title=Pistons win consecutive games for first time since October, beating Trail Blazers 128-122 in OT|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585369|website=ESPN.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 9, 2024}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2026–present)=== On June 29, 2026, Grant was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] along with forward [[Kris Murray]] in exchange for former All-Star [[Ja Morant]]. {{Cite web |title=GRIZZLIES ACQUIRE JERAMI GRANT AND KRIS MURRAY FROM TRAIL BLAZERS |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-jerami-grant-and-kris-murray-from-trail-blazers |date=2026-06-29 |access-date=2026-06-30 |website=NBA.com |language=en-US}} ==National team
